newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission postpones decision on tobacco subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Commission postpones decision on tobacco subsidies.

text.p: The European Commission, divided over how far to go in reforming the European Union's controversial tobacco subsidy programme, agreed on Wednesday to postpone the decision for two weeks, Commission officials said.
They said the Commission was split between those wanting to accept a plan advocated by Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler and those wanting to go further.
Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn won support from four other commissioners for his campaign to phase out the subsidies altogether, officials said.
A Commission spokesman said the EU executive wanted more time to study the impact of the proposals on the farmers who grow tobacco in eight EU states, led by Italy and Greece.
"Obviously it will have a socio-economic impact on producers and on regions, there's no doubt about that," spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida told a news briefing.
"So the commissioners felt they should delve a little bit deeper into this point, and they'd like to give themselves another fortnight to come up with the best possible solution."
Flynn has led a campaign to phase out EU tobacco subsidies, arguing that they compromise the EU's efforts to combat 500,000 smoking-related deaths a year.
But Fischler argues that would put 200,000 farmers and related workers out of jobs without curbing smoking since consumers would simply buy imported products.
He also argues that tobacco farmers would have a hard time diversifying to other products since they generally work on small patches of land that is not suitable for anything else.

Fischler proposed instead targeting money at higher-quality tobacco, offering buyouts to entice farmers to abandon tobacco and doubling the one percent levy on subsidies that is used to finance the EU's anti-smoking efforts.

The Commission divided into three camps on Wednesday, officials said. Those supporting Fischler included President Jacques Santer and Commissioners Yves-Thibault de Silguy, Christos Papoutsis and Marcelino Oreja. Those supporting Flynn included Commissioners Neil Kinnock, Sir Leon Brittan, Karel Van Miert and Ritt Bjerregaard. Several other commissioners said they wanted Fischler's plan to go further, officials said.

The Commission agreed a separate communication drafted by Flynn, however, that outlines new measures the EU and member states could take to discourage smoking, covering issues ranging from health warnings to vending machines.
It will not formally adopt it, however, until the tobacco subsidy proposals are finalised, officials said.
